label: TP
reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value is the user-provided header name (param) which is used in HTML output after encoding, but the encoding is applied to the wrong variable (str instead of param). Alert 2 (java/http-response-splitting): alert-TP — resolved sink value is the user-provided header name (param) which is directly used in the Cookie constructor, creating a potential HTTP response splitting vulnerability. Both alerts are exploitable based on the code analysis showing user input reaching vulnerable sinks.

evidence.note: User input from getHeaderNames() flows through names.nextElement() to param
param is assigned to str, which is used in Cookie creation and HTML output
str (containing user input) is used in new Cookie(...) sink
str (containing user input) is used in HTML response output
